claims.paraphrase: Page title.
Page tagline.
Section heading.
Adding editors needs sign-in email: a connected domain with Email Sending.
Without email sign-in only the owner can sign in.
Section heading.
Every signed-in person is an owner or editor; a developer can add roles.
A site with custom roles shows extra role choices on the screen.
An owner does everything an editor can plus manages the roster; editors cannot change access.
Editors can write and publish; only owners manage access.
The page will not remove or demote the last owner.
Section heading.
At the bottom of the editors screen, fill in name, email, role, and select Add editor.
No email is sent from that action and there is no separate invitation step.
The added person signs in later at the admin with their email and receives a link.
Section heading.
The page lists everyone who can sign in, with Remove in each row and a role button.
Default roles show Make owner or Make editor; custom roles show a dropdown and Change.
Your own row controls are disabled; the last-owner rule is the real lockout guard.
Section heading.
The added person can go to the admin, enter their email, and receive a sign-in link.
Mail can take a while to warm up right after email sign-in is first turned on.
